page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.7xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also register poor to weak results. Conversely, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores consistently placing in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also align with average performance tiers, though the Passmark memory score itself registers in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.7xlarge offers a balanced allocation of compute and memory resources, making it suitable for workloads that can leverage parallel execution to offset the modest single-core performance. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs reduces overhead for deployments that do not require high-speed local disk I/O or hardware acceleration. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that scale across its 32 dedicated cores.
